rows.opus_note: Y has sense-reversing misreadings, e.g. 'μεῖζον μὲν ἐν Υἱῷ' for printed 'μεῖον', 'ἢ ἄρα ἐλάττων' for 'οὐκ ἄρα ἐλάττων', 'ἐκεῖ γὰρ ἐλάττων ὁ Υἱός', plus invented 'φοβούμενον λόγιζον' for 'φόβῳ βαλλόμενον'; X follows the print much more closely.
rows.gemini_note: Y introduces severe sense-changing errors, transcribing 'μεῖζον μὲν ἐν Υἱῷ' instead of 'μεῖον μὲν ἐν Υἱῷ' and 'ἢ σκότος ἐν σκότῳ' instead of 'ἢ σκεῦος ἐν σκεύει'.

rows.opus_note: X reads 'ἱστοριῶν γοῦν τοῦ οἰκείου στέφανον' where the print has 'ἐλάχιστον γοῦν τοῦ οἰκείου ἔργου στέφανον', so it changes a word and drops 'ἔργου'; Y has that line right and keeps the printed 'hæc hæc', and otherwise the two are close.
rows.gemini_note: X replaces 'ἐλάχιστον' with 'ἱστοριῶν' and omits 'ἔργου' in the Greek text ('ἐλάχιστον γοῦν τοῦ οἰκείου ἔργου').

rows.opus_note: X garbles key passages, e.g. 'τὸν δρόμον' for 'τὸν φθόνον', 'αἰτία'/'ἀλήθεια' for 'ἔνδεια'/'ἀσθένεια', 'οὐδὲ βίος' for 'οὐδὲ ἕξις', and 'ἀχώριστος' for the final 'ἄρα μόνος'; Y follows the hand far better, though it has its own errors in lines 1–4 ('αὐτονοῦς' for 'αὐτομονάς').
rows.gemini_note: X severely garbles the text with sense-changing misreadings throughout, including reading 'τὸν φθόνον' as 'τὸν δρόμον' and 'οὐδὲ ἕξις' as 'οὐδὲ βίος'.

rows.opus_note: Y drops 'in hunc modum. Cum dixisset Hieronymus' (which breaks the sentence) and also drops 'vel ut cum doctis sic legam, vehhataim ladonai meod'; X is complete.
rows.gemini_note: Y omits 'in hunc modum. Cum dixisset Hieronymus' and 'vel ut cum doctis sic legam, vehhataim ladonai meod'.

rows.opus_note: The shelfmark painted on the cover reads 'P. 69.' as in X; Y gives a wrong number, 'P. 62.'
rows.gemini_note: Y misreads the shelfmark number 'P. 69.' as 'P. 62.'.

rows.opus_note: X leaves out 'τῶν γεγενημένων πρῶτον ὑμᾶς' and 'μέμνησθε' and misreads 'ἀλλ' ἐκεῖνο ἀπορῶ … πέπεισμαι … ὑπομένειν' (it has 'ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ ἀπορῶ … οἴομαι'); Y matches the manuscript text.
rows.gemini_note: X substitutes numerous words throughout and omits 'γεγενημένων πρῶτον' (col. 1, line 18) and 'πόλιν' (col. 2, line 31).

rows.opus_note: The first line reads 'εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι' as in Y; X invents 'ᾧ δὲ ἀφίενται αἱ πολλαὶ ἁμαρτίαι', and X also has 'μὴ βλέπωσι' where the leaf has 'μὴ ἴδωσι'.
rows.gemini_note: X replaces 'εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ · ἀφέωνταί σου' with 'ᾧ δὲ ἀφίενται αἱ πολλαὶ' in lines 1–2, omitting Christ's words to the woman.

rows.opus_note: Y omits the whole line 'καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι αὐτοῖς τῶν εὐδαιμόνων διὰ τὸ ἁβροδίαιτον', has 'σταδιεῖς' where the leaf has 'ἀθληταί', and garbles the last lines.
rows.gemini_note: X inserts printed-edition text not found on the leaf ('καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι αὐτοῖς τῶν εὐδαιμόνων διὰ τὸ ἁβροδίαιτον') and misses manuscript readings like 'σταδιεῖς'.

rows.opus_note: The opening lines read 'εἰ δὲ χωρίς ἐστε παιδείας ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασι πάντες, ἄρα νόθοι ἐστὲ καὶ οὐχ υἱοί… τοὺς μὲν τῆς σαρκός' as in Y; X turns them into nonsense ('κομιδῆ χοι νόμασι πεντάς… μόθοι ἄγε καὶ ἐχλοί… ποιοῦμεν').
rows.gemini_note: X severely garbles lines 1–3 with nonsensical readings such as 'κομιδῆ χοινόμασι πεντάς' and 'ἆρα μόθοι ἄγε καὶ ἐχλοί' instead of 'ἧς μέτοχοι γεγόνασι πάντες' and 'ἄρα νόθοι ἐστὲ καὶ οὐχ υἱοί'.

rows.opus_note: The print has 'ἤλυθον· ἔνθ’' and 'ἤλυθον· ἔνθα', which Y gives correctly; X has 'ἦλθον' twice and 'ἔνθ’ κελαινώπεσσι', small form errors that do not change the sense.
rows.gemini_note: X prints 'ἦλθον' instead of 'ἤλυθον' twice and 'ἔνθ’' for 'ἔνθα'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf is a single column of Aristotle's Topics that Y follows closely ('ἀναιροῦντι μὲν οὖν, καθάπερ εἴρηται'). X garbles the wording, invents a second column and repeats a fake margin note ('τὸ δὲ πρὸς τί, ὡς τὸ διπλάσιον') six times.
rows.gemini_note: X severely garbles the Greek text throughout (e.g. transcribing 'τυφλότης ἀναιρεθείσης, ὄψις ἀναιρεῖται' for 'τυφλότης ἀναισθησία τίς, ἡ ὄψις ἂν αἴσθησις') and repeats spurious marginal tags six times, whereas Y is highly accurate.

rows.opus_note: X matches the Greek, the Latin and the 'γρ. εἰ γὰρ μηδενὶ…' margin note. Y drops that note, corrupts terms ('ζῶον ὅτι σήπει' for 'ζῶον, ἐπιστήμη, ἄγριον') and leaves out the Latin clause 'At pro certo ac concesso habebatur nullum consequi: verum'.
rows.gemini_note: Y corrupts the Greek text with severe misreadings such as 'ζῶον ὅτι σήπει' for 'ἐπιστήμη' and omits the Latin clause 'est. At pro certo ac concesso habebatur nullum consequi: verum'.

rows.opus_note: X reads the printed words better ('γρῖφος', 'γαλιψὸς καβεῖα', 'δύο'). Y misreads many of them, often putting λ for δ ('χρίσιος', 'λύω', 'λίδυμος', 'λείπνον'), which changes the dictionary entries.
rows.gemini_note: Y systematically misreads initial delta as lambda (e.g., 'λαίειν' for 'δαίειν', 'λεί' for 'δεῖ') and misidentifies 'δαίμων' as 'λαίμαργον'.

rows.opus_note: Y follows the Demosthenes text on the leaf ('οὔτε γὰρ ὡς δοκεῖ καὶ φήσειέ τις ἂν μὴ σκοπῶν ἀκριβῶς'; column 2 starts 'ἀπὸ τούτων δέοι διοικεῖν'). X garbles it ('ὡς δόξει καὶ φοβερός ἐστι'), starts column 2 with the wrong lines and invents scholia passages.
rows.gemini_note: X heavily garbles the Greek text across both columns and omits key passages, including the reference to the Paeonians and Illyrians ('τό γε Παιόνων καὶ τὸ Ἰλλυριῶν').

rows.opus_note: The leaf is illegible and X says so honestly. Y invents readable Latin sentences ('et erat in illo tempore in civitate quodam homo'), though Y reads the foliation 'n. 69' correctly where X has '169'.
rows.gemini_note: X omits the legible opening lines ('autem fuit die una').

rows.opus_note: Y matches the rubric ('τοῦ ἰατροῦ τοῦ Ἰωάννου') and the opening ('πρὸς τὰς ἀπατούσας'), and keeps the run of red rubric headings on sounds and signs. X's wording is largely invented ('πρὸς ἁπάσας τῶν μεθόδων') and it repeats a garbled rubric.
rows.gemini_note: X heavily garbles the text with invented phrases like 'καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν πνευμάτων' and omits key logical terms like 'βλίτυρι'.

rows.opus_note: Y gets key lines right ('πόλεμον ἔχωμεν ὦ μειρακίσκοι', 'ὑπὸ τῶν ὀλυμπιονικῶν', 'ἀνδρός· λογγῖνος'). X misreads them into different sense ('πόλιν οὐκ ἔχομεν ᾧ μικροὶ', 'πήχη τὰς μήκωνας') and adds a page number '21'. Both are rough in the middle.
rows.gemini_note: Y heavily confabulates text across the page, inventing phrases such as 'βενεδίκτοις' for 'βενδιδίοις' and omitting 'ἐν τῷ Πειραιεῖ'.

rows.opus_note: Both texts give the verse, speaker labels and notes c–e exactly; they differ only in indentation markup.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions faithfully record the leaf with identical text from 'The truths you mention' to the footnotes, differing only in markup conventions.

rows.opus_note: The two texts are word-for-word identical ('become guardian of that ruler's son', '481 (Gaspar), 477 (L. Schmidt),'); only the tags differ.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions are equally faithful to the leaf from 'NEMEAN I' to '477 (L. Schmidt)', differing only in markup conventions.

rows.opus_note: The two texts are identical, including all three footnotes ('See Rogers, Introduction, p. ix.'); only the formatting differs.
rows.gemini_note: Both transcriptions faithfully record the text ('The Peace was exhibited at the great city Dionysia') and footnotes without textual errors.

rows.opus_note: Y swaps printed wording for invented phrases, e.g. 'ἀπαντῶντες ... περὶ τοῦ ἐγκλήματος' for 'ἀγῶνες ... ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος', 'ἠρώτα δὲ πρῶτον αὐτὸς' for 'καὶ περὶ αὐτοῦ γε πρότερον', and ends with 'ἐννέα γὰρ' where the leaf has 'ἀνάλωμα'; X is closer throughout, despite its own errors.
rows.gemini_note: Y severely corrupts the text with numerous fabricated readings, replacing 'ἣν ἐκέκτητο' with 'μὴ ἐκπίπτωσι' and 'ἀγῶνες αὐτῷ' with 'ἀπαντῶντες'.

rows.opus_note: Both are heavily garbled: X has the wrong page number '85' (leaf reads 58) and invents 'Καὶ τοὶ δὲ αἱ γῆς καὶ λίμνας'; Y invents 'ὕδωρ ὄν τε' and 'σὺν γὰρ ἀφανισμῷ ...', but gets 'καίτοι φαίη ἄν τις καὶ ἄλλως' and the closing lines right.
rows.gemini_note: X repeatedly hallucinates and garbles the text, fabricating phrases such as 'πνεύματος αὐτὰ ῥήξαντος' and reading 'λαίμαψ τινος ἀσεβείας' for 'λοιμοῦ τινος ἢ σεισμοῦ'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf opens 'ἔφη ἴσμεν μή σε τὸ ἄλγος' and closes 'βεβηκυῖα· ὡς ἂν μὴ ἀνεγερθείη', as Y gives; X starts with an invented 'ἐμὲ ἰσχυρῶς ἐκίνησε' and largely fabricates the text, though Y also wrongly treats the facing page's text as this leaf's margin.
rows.gemini_note: X heavily hallucinates the text, opening with 'ἐμὲ ἰσχυρῶς ἐκίνησε' instead of 'ἔφη· ἴσμεν μή σε τὸ ἄλγος' and fabricating passages throughout.

rows.opus_note: The two texts are essentially identical; X keeps the printed misprint 'nnreasonable' and Y silently corrects it to 'unreasonable'.
rows.gemini_note: X faithfully preserves the leaf's printed reading 'nnreasonable', whereas Y normalizes it to 'unreasonable'.

rows.opus_note: The leaf begins 'ἐπειδὴ δὲ μετέωρον τὸ λυπηρὸν ἦν, ἀπεκρίνατο' and later has 'κομήτας', matching Y; X's 'Ἐπειδὴ ὑστέρησε τὸ πλῆθος' and its Achilles/Hector/Odysseus narrative are invented.
rows.gemini_note: X invents an imaginary Trojan War narrative mentioning Hector, Odysseus, and Helen ('Ἑλένην ὡς ἀποδοθῆναι'), whereas the manuscript actually discusses astronomical and meteorological phenomena such as comets ('κομήτας').

rows.opus_note: Both texts include all of the leaf's text, but Y transcribes every left half-column before every right one, which breaks sentences across sections (e.g. 'Attamen omnes homines qui,' is separated from 'viderunt majestatem meam'); X keeps the reading order, though it has 'quoddam' for 'quodam'.
rows.gemini_note: Y transcribes down the columns instead of across the three horizontal sections, splitting sentences such as 'Attamen omnes homines qui, viderunt majestatem meam' across the column break.

rows.opus_note: Y fabricates most of the first dozen lines, including the invented number 'ὑπὸ Ἀθηναίων ἐφάνησαν πεντακόσιαι' where the leaf has 'ὑπὲρ ἥμισυ Κᾶρες ἐφάνησαν', and garbles the Agamemnon sentence; X follows the Thucydides text apart from its first line.
rows.gemini_note: Y severely corrupts the text with invented passages (e.g. 'ἐφάνησαν πεντακόσιαι') and omits Agamemnon ('Ἀγαμέμνων').

rows.opus_note: Both texts reproduce all 16 lines of Peace and the footnote correctly; the only differences are formatting and the placement of line numbers.
